17:19 Local Time, 13:19 GMT, 18:49 IST: It was the moving day and the Test has moved in Zimbabwe's direction. They lead by 291 runs, have 3 wickets in hand and two full days of cricket. Afghanistan started the day with their batters showing some resistance and seeing off the first hour, but the two leggies, Cremer and Masekasa, quickly took the last four wickets in the second hour to give Zimbabwe a 122-run lead. Their batters lost wickets at regular intervals, losing five of them in the final session, but still managed to stretch the lead thanks once again to Taylor's fifty, his fourth 50+ score in the series. Afghanistan's pace trio did most of the damage, taking 6 of the 7 wickets to fall, but they are still way behind in the game. They will need to pick up the final three wickets quickly tomorrow and their batters will have to chase a big total on a pitch that is proving tricky. Join us for all the action from day 4. 13:41 local, 09:41 GMT, 15:11 IST: 418 to win the Test match and the series for Afghanistan. Massive credit to Zimbabwe's tail for their incredible resistance and frustrating their opponents by killing enough time in the middle. Cremer was happy to play the second fiddle with Muzarabani, but took matters into his own hands after the latter's departure. The lead is big enough, but if you bat sensibly, there are plenty of runs on offer. A light roller is being used currently and Afghanistan should take plenty of confidence from the batting grit on display today morning. "If their tail can bat for so long, why can't we?" should and could be the message. Let's see how they approach this. Back in 10...
